Q: How to track all remote Git branches as local branches? A:

Update Q1 2020: Mohsen Abasi proposes in the comments, based on the 2014 slm's answer, the simpler alternative:

for i in $(git branch -r | grep -vE "HEAD|master" | sed 's/^[ ]\+//');  do git switch --track $i; done

And it uses $() instead of obsolete backticks.

As I mention in another old answer, using git for-each-ref is probably faster.
And I would use the new (Git 2.23+) git switch command, which replaces the confusing git checkout.

for i in $(git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:short)' \
   --no-merged=origin/HEAD refs/remotes/origin); do \
      git switch --track $i; \
done

That way, no grep needed.

If you really need to avoid "hardwiring" the rmeote name "origin", you can try to use upstream:

remote=$(git for-each-ref --format='%(upstream:remotename)' "$(git symbolic-ref -q HEAD)")

for i in $(git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:short)' \
  --no-merged="$remote/HEAD" "refs/remotes/$remote"); do
    git switch --track "$i"
done

Note that it means "the remote associated with my current branch", not "the default remote".
Git has several notions that can influence a remote choice, such as branch.<name>.remote, remote.pushDefault, and even checkout.defaultRemote: there is no single global remote that universally replaces "origin".

Old (2011) original answer:

Here is my one-liner I use (in a bash shell, tested with msysgit1.7.4):

For copy-paste:

remote=origin ; for brname in `git branch -r | grep $remote | grep -v master | grep -v HEAD | awk '{gsub(/^[^\/]+\//,"",$1); print $1}'`; do git branch --set-upstream-to $remote/$brname $brname; done

For more readability:

remote=origin ; // put here the name of the remote you want
for brname in `
  git branch -r | grep $remote | grep -v master | grep -v HEAD 
  | awk '{gsub(/^[^\/]+\//,"",$1); print $1}'
  `; do 
  git branch --set-upstream-to $remote/$brname $brname; 
done

  • it will only select upstream branches from the remote you specify in the remote variable (it can be 'origin' or whatever name you have set for one of the remotes of your current Git repo).

  • it will extract the name of the branch: origin/a/Branch/Name => a/Branch/Name through the awk expression.

  • it will set the upstream branch through --set-upstream-to (or -u), not --track:
    The advantage is that, if the branch already exists, it won't fail and it won't change that branch origin, it will only configure the branch.xxx.(remote|merge) setting.

    branch.aBranchName.remote=origin
branch.aBranchName.merge=refs/heads/a/Branch/Name

That command will create local branches for all remote upstream branches, and set their remote and merge setting to that remote branch.

Q: How do I exit Vim? A:

Exiting Vim

First press Esc to make sure you're in normal mode (not insert/visual). Then:

Goal Command
Quit (no unsaved changes) :q Enter
Save and quit :wq or :x or ZZ
Quit, discarding changes :q! or ZQ
Quit all open windows/tabs :qa (add ! to discard)

The leading : opens the command line, so nothing happens until you hit Enter.

If :q complains E37: No write since last change, you have unsaved edits, use :wq to keep them or :q! to throw them away.

If you're stuck because the terminal appears frozen, you may have hit Ctrl+S; press Ctrl+Q to resume.

Q: I've been trying to apply Hough transformation for line detection on an image of rails. But I'm facing problems A:

Hough Line Transform can be a little tricky when the input image contains noise, uneven lighting, or edges that are not clearly defined. I’d try applying grayscale conversion, Gaussian blur, and Canny edge detection before running the transform. Adjusting the threshold and minimum line length can also make a big difference in the detected results. Protopond.

Q: PyTorch installation fails with incomplete-download errors on Linux Mint A:

So apparently, it’s not network-related. I installed the CPU version of PyTorch, and it worked.

Installation:
pip3 install torch torchvision --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu

Not really what I wanted, but it’ll do for the time being, until someone else runs into the same issue.
